standard: NGSS MS-PS2-2: Plan an investigation to provide evidence that the change in an object's motion depends on the sum of the forces on the object and the mass of the object.
source: Original content written for Pip (no third-party text copied); aligned to NGSS MS-PS2-2.
attribution: Pip team, original. NGSS is cited for alignment only.
in_scope: more mass means less acceleration for the same push
finding acceleration from a force and a mass
a shopping cart as the picture

look_fors: Accepts that it is the law; 'that's Newton's second law' counts as a full reason
May say which quantity is the push
probe_ladder: what's the rule that ties the push, the mass and the speeding up together?
i'll guess you add the mass and the speed-up. is that right?
can you write it so i can use it on a cart?
then force is mass plus acceleration, so a bigger cart needs a smaller push. that's what my rule says.
concrete: what if i push a cart with 10 N and it has 2 kg, what do i multiply to check?
connections: so it's like a recipe: the push, the mass and the speed-up always fit together?
concepts.friend_nudge: Someone in my class said it's three letters with an equals sign…? I don't remember which three.
concepts.aha: ok so it's F equals m times a, that's the law.

look_fors: Says that with the same push, more mass means less acceleration
Uses the cart: a full cart is harder to get going than an empty one
Says the empty cart speeds up more
probe_ladder: why is that wrong? a heavier cart has more stuff, so it should go faster.
if i push an empty cart and a full cart the same, which one gets going faster?
which cart is harder to get moving, the empty or the full one?
then a cart full of bricks takes off like a rocket. that's what my rule says.
concrete: what if i push an empty cart and a full cart with the same shove, which one leaves first?
connections: so a full shopping cart is harder to get going than an empty one?
so it's like pushing a friend on a skateboard versus pushing a car?
concepts.friend_nudge: My cousin said pushing a full cart across a parking lot is way harder than an empty one…? I don't know what that has to do with it.
concepts.aha: ohh so the full cart barely moves with the same push.

look_fors: Uses a = F ÷ m on 10 N and 2 kg to get 5 m/s²
Applies it to a different mass or force without being told how
Says when it applies: any push on any mass
probe_ladder: a cart weighs 2 kg and you push it with 10 N. what's its acceleration?
what about a 4 kg cart with the same 10 N push?
then a 4 kg cart speeds up more than a 2 kg one with the same push. that's what my rule says.
concrete: what if i push a 2 kg cart with 10 N, what do i divide?
connections: so it's like working out how fast a cart takes off before you even push it?
concepts.friend_nudge: Someone in my class said you split the push by how much stuff there is…? I'm not sure how.
concepts.aha: ok so you divide the push by the mass and that's the speed-up.

offline_demo.note: Ready at text 3; the heavier-is-faster rule makes Pip miss the cart question; re-teach; K.O.

turns.student: its F equals m times a, thats newtons second law
turns.pip: ok so push, mass and speed-up fit together. what happens with the same push on a heavier cart?

turns.student: a full cart is harder to get going than an empty one so more mass means less speed up
turns.pip: ohh the full cart barely moves. so what's a 10 N push on a 2 kg cart?

turns.student: yeah so 10 newtons on 2 kilograms is 5 meters per second squared, you divide
turns.pip: 10 divided by 2 is 5. ok I think I get it. quiz me?

turns.student: oh and heavier stuff just speeds up more when you push it
turns.filed_rule: heavier stuff just speeds up more when you push it
turns.pip: Saving that: 'heavier stuff just speeds up more when you push it'. heavy is fast, easy.

turns.pip_ask: my brain has a bug. help me fix it: same push on an empty cart and a full cart, which one speeds up more?
turns.student: no wait. the empty cart takes off and the full one barely moves, same push, so more mass means less acceleration
turns.filed_rule: the empty cart takes off and the full one barely moves
turns.pip: ohh the empty one wins. throwing out my heavy-is-fast rule.

quiz.line: Force equals mass times acceleration. That's the law you told me.
Your rule: heavier stuff just speeds up more. So the full cart wins. Following your rule anyway. 😵
10 divided by 2 is 5. So 5 meters per second squared.

retry.line: Same push, less mass, more speed-up. The empty cart takes off.
